name: Planning Poker
description: This project describes 'Planning Poker' a digital card game designed to help empower agile and scrum development teams to collectively set their sprint goals. Using anonymous pointing, Planning Poker helps to elicit productive conversations across the team to create shared ownership, knowledge, and understanding.
rawDescription: This project describes 'Planning Poker' a digital card game designed to help empower agile and scrum development teams to collectively set their sprint goals. Using anonymous pointing, Planning Poker helps to elicit productive conversations across the team to create shared ownership, knowledge, and understanding.
highLevelGoals: Ensure that all team members can contribute equally to estimating user stories without bias, fostering shared ownership and alignment on sprint goals.
Allow the Product Owner to define and enforce sprint goals while ensuring the team understands and commits to them through collaborative estimation.
Enable Development Team Members to engage in anonymous, structured estimation to reduce estimation bias and promote collective understanding of user stories.
lowLevelGoals: Enable the Scrum Master to set up estimation parameters such as story point scales, estimation methods, and bias mitigation strategies.
Allow the Scrum Master to trigger estimation sessions with pre-configured rules and user story sets.
Enable Development Team Members to submit estimates anonymously to prevent social bias during estimation sessions.
Enable each team member to submit their individual estimate for a user story using the configured estimation method.
Enable the team to vote or agree on final estimates after anonymous submission to ensure consensus.
Allow the Product Owner to create and define sprint goals for the upcoming sprint.
Allow the Product Owner to map user stories to sprint goals and enforce goal alignment during estimation.
Enable the team to review estimation outcomes and collaboratively refine estimates through discussion or voting mechanisms.
Allow the team to engage in post-estimation discussions to clarify ambiguities and adjust estimates based on collective knowledge.
Allow the Scrum Master to verify that user stories being estimated are mapped to defined sprint goals and to flag mismatches for discussion.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are appropriate for a Planning Poker system, as they align with typical roles in agile/scrum teams. No contradictions or omissions are observed.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-defined and align with the description of Planning Poker. They focus on functional aspects such as transparent estimation, prioritized sprint goal alignment, and collaborative knowledge sharing. No contradictions or omissions are observed.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and actors, covering all necessary functional aspects of Planning Poker. However, there is a minor omission regarding the Product Owner's ability to prioritize the backlog before sprint planning, which is implied in the high-level goal "Support Prioritized Sprint Goal Alignment." Additionally, while the low-level goals are comprehensive, they could benefit from explicitly mentioning the system's support for different estimation methods (e.g., Fibonacci sequence, T-shirt sizing) and the ability to export or save session results for future reference.
